source: HttpWebSocketResponseActionHandler.writeWebSocketFrame's listener: a scripted message whose write fails because the client has gone (ExceptionHandling.clientGoneException) is the DEBUG entry `client left before WebSocket message {} was sent:{}for request:{}`, with the cause's class and message. Here the client stops reading a 42 MB message (rendered by a Velocity template, so the expectation and its log entries stay small) and WriteStallTimeoutHandler closes the channel under it, so the pending write fails with Netty's StacklessClosedChannelException

steps.note: a 42 MB text message to a WebSocket client that stops reading: cut after a second, while the message is being written

tcp.text:
GET /ws HTTP/1.1
Host: {{host}}
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13

steps.note: the stall WARN, then the DEBUG entry for message 1 (no `sent WebSocket message` entry, and message 2 is never written)

mask.reason: what waits for the client depends on socket buffers (response_write_stall_websocket)
